title: Fee Ledger Worksheet: Amount of a Billing-Error Correction on a Bluegate Tenant Protection Plan
content:
**Rule.** On a Bluegate Tenant Protection Plan, the charge examined is the latest protection fee charge posted on the plan. That charge is in billing error when it is a second charge for a billing period already charged on the plan — that is, when the plan's fee ledger shows two or more protection fee charges for the billing period of that latest charge. The billing-error correction credits the charge in error in full, with a billing-error correction credit referencing that charge. The amount of the correction is the amount of the charge in error, rounded to the cent only once, on the final amount credited.

## Worksheet lines

1. *Charge examined* — the latest protection fee charge posted on the plan's fee ledger, with its amount and its billing period.
2. *Charges for that period* — the number of protection fee charges on the plan for the same billing period.
3. *Charge in error* — the amount of the charge examined when line 2 is two or more; nothing when line 2 is one, since a period charged once carries no billing error.
4. *Correction credited* — line 3, rounded to the cent.

## Worked example (hypothetical ledger)

| Fee ledger entry | Billing period starting | Amount |
| --- | --- | --- |
| protection fee charge, posted 1 June | 1 June | 29.00 |
| protection fee charge, posted 4 June | 1 June | 29.00 |

The latest charge (posted 4 June) is for the period starting 1 June, which the ledger shows charged twice. Line 3 is 29.00, and the correction credited is 29.00, referencing the charge posted 4 June.

Had the ledger shown only the charge of 1 June for that period, the latest charge would be the only charge for its period; line 3 would be nothing and there would be no amount to credit.
